column1: # Where each gloss in lex-fr.tsv was read.
# lemma | pos | tgt | sources | quote | stands
# The gloss is the English word a French word is woven for, and the tooltip
# prints it back: it is the claim every reader meets first. Every other claim
# the pack makes about a word names its entry — genders in fr-genders.tsv,
# plurals in fr-plurals.tsv, verb forms in fr-verb-forms.tsv, etymologies in
# fr-cousins.tsv — and the gloss named none until 2026-10-08, as the Latin
# and Old English glosses named none until la-glosses.tsv and ang-glosses.tsv.
# Every row is read, all 356: the 178 nouns, 81 verbs, 57 adjectives, 22
# adverbs, 13 numerals and 5 interjections. Each was read in the rendered
# page of the word's English Wiktionary entry, in its French section: a
# script took the definition lines under each heading of the row's part of
# speech — the items of the list below its headword line, with the usage
# examples, quotations and synonyms beneath them set aside — and drafted the
# first that holds the row's English word, and every quote was read against
# its page. Where that first line is another sense, the quote is the row's:
# question's first is "(historical, chiefly with the definite article)
# question (interrogation by torture)", and its line quotes the sense that
# A page holds every word of one spelling, so a quote is from this word's
# own part of speech where the page has it. Three rows' words have none of
# theirs, and their lines quote the heading the page gives them: seul, woven
# for "alone" among the adverbs, is an adjective in French, as English
# "alone" is both; premier, "first", is an ordinal adjective, not a numeral;
# and s’il vous plaît is a phrase, not an interjection.
# The title is the word as Wiktionary's address writes it: without a
# homograph's number — mort² is read in mort, under its adjective — with a
# straight apostrophe, as Wiktionary titles aujourd'hui, and with an
# underscore for a space, so that each source stays one word of the field:
# wikt:fr:au_revoir, wikt:fr:s'il_vous_plaît. A noun cites the entry its
# gender was read in, which for every French noun is its own.
# Blank where the quote holds the row's English word. Otherwise it names the
# word of the quote that stands for it, because the English word is not in
# the entry. Seven rows need one: marin for "sailor" is "seaman", cheveu for
# "hair" "a headhair", limier for "hound" "sleuth; bloodhound, limer", tissu
# for "cloth" "fabric", rapide for "quick" "fast, rapid", beau for
# day", its interjection's line. The page's noun, "greetings; hello (general
# salutation)", holds the word, and is the word as a thing one says, "dire
# bonjour"; the row is the interjection.
# One row no definition gave. tenir debout, woven for "stand" until
# 2026-10-08, is "(informal) to hold water, to be valid, to make sense":
# what an argument does, "ça ne tient pas debout", that doesn't hold water,
# and not what a person does. A person standing is debout, "standing, stood
# up, upright", and "stand" is être debout now, whose own entry is "stand
# (be upright, support oneself on the feet in an erect position)", the shape
# of Spanish estar de pie, Italian stare in piedi and Portuguese estar de pé.
# se tenir debout has no entry, and lever's reflexive, "to rise, stand up",
# is standing up, not standing. The learner's tenir debout card is
# withdrawn: WITHDRAWN in src/core/renames.ts keeps it.
# Three quotes are true and say less than the row is woven for, and are
# recorded rather than changed. cheveu is one hair, and its entry's usage
# note says English's mass noun "hair" is French's plural, cheveux. asseoir
# is "(transitive) to sit (someone) down, to seat, make sit", where English's
# intransitive "sit" is the reflexive's, "to sit down, sit up, take a seat".
# And monter, woven for "rise", gives the word only in a figurative sense,
# "to rise (get to a higher figurative position ...)", where the climb is
# "to ascend, go higher". The first two are calls in TODO.md.
# tests/tools/glosses.test.ts requires every row of lex-fr.tsv to have a line
# here citing its own word's entry, whose quote holds its English word or the
# stand-in it names, and fails on a line outliving its row.
